clue.text: At sea, read lots in navigational guide

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A navigator reads lots of material out on the ocean to find the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the navigation story but is the anagram signal: READ LOTS rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A guiding star used by sailors to steer by, especially the pole star.

clue.text: Departed from hospital, but not going right

parts.note: departed means went away, left
a ward is a room in a hospital

explanation.surface: A patient discharged from hospital is not recovering as hoped.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading towards the opposite side to the right is moving in that direction.

clue.text: Died, going wrong with act showing reckless heroism

parts.note: erring means straying or going wrong
to do is to act

explanation.surface: Someone died after a botched stunt meant as a display of daring.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring deeds; foolhardy bravery of the swashbuckling kind.

clue.text: Where to find book left, and female?

definitions.text: Where to find book left, and female?

parts.words: Where to find book left, and female?
parts.note: a book is put away on a ledge; an unmarried woman past the usual age was once said to be left 'on the' same thing

explanation.walkthrough: The old phrase 'left on the shelf' described a woman thought too old to marry; the question mark flags the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is where books are stored, and the idiom places neglected spinsters there too.

clue.text: Pain — is right treatment this?

indicators.note: giving letters a treatment means working them over into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether a common pill is the correct remedy for pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges PAIN, IS and R; the whole clue then also describes the answer, a painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: A common analgesic tablet, the obvious treatment for a headache.

clue.text: Impostor displays activity and enthusiasm

parts.note: a hum of activity, a busy buzz
a bug is a craze or enthusiasm, as in 'the travel bug'

explanation.surface: A fraud shows lots of energy and keenness.
explanation.definitionFit: A humbug is a sham or fraud, a person who deceives.

clue.text: In pure perplexity, composer's seen to fill in with padding

indicators.note: one piece sits in the confusion of another, so it is placed inside
perplexity is confusion, so the letters of pure are muddled

parts.note: Gustav Holst, English composer of The Planets

explanation.surface: A composer appears baffled while stuffing cushions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal, not a link; 'perplexity' scrambles the four-letter word into UPER, split around the English composer of The Planets.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster is to stuff and cover furniture with soft material.

clue.text: Living at home, ask to go outside

indicators.note: the word for ask must surround the other piece

parts.note: beg means ask
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone living with parents is asked to step outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence; a living thing is a being.

clue.text: Mischievous girl portrayed in Enigma Variation

indicators.note: a variation is an altered version, so the letters of enigma are rearranged

explanation.surface: A playful girl is depicted in Elgar's Enigma Variations.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface alludes to Elgar's Enigma Variations, each a portrait of a friend; 'Variation' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamine is an impish, boyishly slim young woman.

clue.text: Melodic fragment from Stravinsky's first, of course

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the composer's name is taken

parts.note: natch is slang for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: A snippet of tune taken from a Stravinsky piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatch is a short burst of song or music.

clue.text: Short run in appearance in silly play

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a face is an outward appearance, as in 'on the face of it'
run shortened to its abbreviation R, as on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: A brief run of a daft comedy on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A farce is a comic play built on absurd situations.

clue.text: Religion takes me in paths out of the normal

indicators.note: letters out of their normal order are rearranged

explanation.surface: Faith leads me down unconventional paths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the normal' rearranges ME, IN and PATHS.
explanation.definitionFit: A belief that God is identical with the universe and nature, a theological doctrine.

clue.text: Don't anticipate being in trouble after delay

indicators.note: the trouble piece follows the delay piece

parts.note: to wait is to delay
for it means about to be punished, as in 'you're for it now'

explanation.surface: Advice not to jump the gun when trouble looms after a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For it' is British slang for being in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhortation to be patient and hold back until something happens.

clue.text: Emblem and name required to start computer session

parts.note: a logo is an emblem

explanation.surface: A badge and username are needed to sign into a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain access to a system by entering credentials.

clue.text: Group of soldiers cut short prescribed exercise etc.

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its last letter

parts.note: a regiment is a unit of soldiers

explanation.surface: A soldiers' unit has its drill programme curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of diet, exercise or treatment.

clue.text: Old soldier not usually seen on mount Athos, for example

definitions.text: Old soldier not usually seen on mount
definitions.meaning: a soldier armed with a musket, an infantryman rather than a horseman
Athos is one of Dumas's three heroes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount Athos' suggests the Greek holy mountain, but Athos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical foot soldier carrying a musket; Athos, Porthos and Aramis are the famous trio.

clue.text: Fast car is what attracts attention? Stepped on it!

parts.note: 'ho!' is a cry to attract attention
trod means stepped on

explanation.surface: A speedy car turns heads, and its driver floored the pedal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stepped on it' sounds like speeding but simply means trod.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot rod is a car modified for high speed.

clue.text: Retiring? Succeeded in getting expenses

parts.note: an outgoing official is one retiring from office
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone retiring finds the costs mounting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests shy, the opposite of sociable, but here means leaving office.
explanation.definitionFit: Money spent; payments going out of an account.

clue.text: Neat present for daughter

parts.note: here means present
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tidy gift for one's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is an old word for cattle, not tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hereford is a breed of beef cattle, and neat is an archaic term for bovine animals.

clue.text: Bit suspiciously at first into fungus

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a morel is an edible fungus

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Someone nibbles warily into a mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A small piece, especially of food.

clue.text: Body of soldiers runs out of restraint

indicators.note: one piece is removed from the other

parts.note: a leg-iron is a shackle
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A troop escapes from its shackles.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman legion was a large military unit.

clue.text: Rubbish in the entrance can be a killer

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Trash left at the gateway may prove deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord or wire used to strangle a victim, so a murderous instrument.

clue.text: Enterprising Indian chief?

definitions.meaning: keen and dynamic, ready to push forward
read as a whimsical Native American name

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a playful made-up chief's name; the question mark signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambitious and dynamic in business.

clue.text: Make a ton in style

parts.note: to form is to make

explanation.surface: Scoring a century in fine fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a ton' suggests a cricketer's hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Layout or arrangement; the way something is presented.

clue.text: At the proper moment, put chalk here

definitions.meaning: exactly on time, at the right signal
a snooker player chalks the tip of the stick, so chalk goes on it

explanation.definitionFit: Like an actor entering at the prompt, it means precisely when needed.

clue.text: Large container, worthy companion to another

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British award
another container, an urn

explanation.surface: A big vessel is a fine partner for a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, Companion of Honour, is a British order; 'another' means another container.
explanation.definitionFit: A large metal milk can, as used on farms.

clue.text: Bagman pleased to receive several pounds

parts.note: glad means pleased
a stone is fourteen pounds in British weight

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman is happy to receive some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' suggests money but is weight: a stone is 14 lb. The Victorian Prime Minister gave his name to the Gladstone bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The statesman lent his name to a hinged travelling case, so he is a man with a bag.

clue.text: Part of flower — confirm it's round head of plant

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to seal a deal is to confirm it

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Checking a plant's flowerhead component.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepal is a leaflike part of a flower's outer calyx.

clue.text: Raty's friend gets new house in Cornish town

indicators.note: one piece takes in the other

parts.note: Mole is Ratty's friend in The Wind in the Willows

indicators.note: a new version of the word, rearranged

explanation.surface: The Wind in the Willows character moves into a fresh home in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's clue has Ratty, the Water Rat; 'new' rearranges the dwelling into USEHO and 'gets' means the Willows animal swallows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing village near Penzance in Cornwall, a place in south-west England.

clue.text: I for a change must appear in panto horse

indicators.note: one letter is changed for another in the word

explanation.surface: An actor must take a turn in the pantomime horse costume.
explanation.walkthrough: Panto is British pantomime, a Christmas stage show often featuring a two-person horse costume; I replaces its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a piebald or spotted horse.

clue.text: Sacred Hindu text — outbursts when false plural is seen

indicators.note: a mock Latin plural replaces the English plural ending

parts.note: tantrums are outbursts of temper

explanation.surface: Fits of temper erupt when a sacred text is misquoted in the plural.
explanation.walkthrough: Treat TANTRUM as Latin: its plural ending -UMS becomes -A, as in datum, data.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantra is a scripture of Hindu or Buddhist mysticism.

clue.text: Adored by fans, though I did lose badly

indicators.note: badly means poorly arranged, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sportsman is worshipped by supporters despite a heavy defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Worshipped or revered like a star by followers.
